description: Compute the potential-determining free-energy step for OER on IrO2(110) under the Computational Hydrogen Electrode model.
user_prompt: Compute the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) reaction profile on the IrO2(110) rutile surface (space group P4_2/mnm) using the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) under the Computational Hydrogen Electrode (CHE) model at U = 0 V vs RHE. Build the CHE free-energy ladder for the four proton-coupled electron-transfer steps (* -> *OH -> *O -> *OOH -> O2) and identify the potential-determining step. Report the free energy of the potential-determining PCET step, delta_G_rds = max(delta_G_1..4) (in eV).

references: Rossmeisl, Qu, Zhu, Kroes & Norskov, J. Electroanal. Chem. 607, 83-89 (2007)
Ping, Galli & Goddard, J. Phys. Chem. C 119, 11570 (2015)
method.modeling: Use a rutile IrO2(110) slab with 4-5 trilayers, vacuum >= 18 Angstrom, and cus-site cycling through *OH, *O, and *OOH intermediates. Build the CHE free-energy ladder at U = 0 V vs RHE for * -> *OH -> *O -> *OOH -> O2, and identify delta_G_rds from the four PCET steps.

key_parameters.free_energy_corrections: CHE with ZPE and entropy corrections at 298 K

method.rationale: Rossmeisl et al. report a theoretical overpotential of 0.56 V for OER on oxygen-covered IrO2(110), with OOH* formation as the potential-determining step, corresponding to delta_G_rds = 1.79 eV at U = 0 V. The corresponding overpotential is the derived quantity eta = delta_G_rds/e - 1.23 V = 0.56 V, while the benchmark scores only delta_G_rds. The +/-0.3 eV absolute tolerance covers HOO* correction choices, low- versus high-coverage IrO2(110) values, and functional/U sensitivity.
